items.title: Hal Galper interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 27, 2022
items.q: I was playing in a house band with Sonny Stitt, amazing gig for two weeks.

ctx.x: So you learn the information in school, you learn how to use it in the apprenticeship system. All right? That’s the only place to learn is the apprenticeship system. You have to play the stuff. You have to try it out and you have to be playing with a master. You can’t — David Baker said, “You don’t learn anything playing with your peers.” You have to play — and all the masters that I played with, apprenticed with, they all had awe. They were awesome. And if they told you do something you stood up and saluted and…

the next level and there’s a whole different set of questions and answers. It just never stops. And there’s a musical structure that goes right along with it. That’s how the discipline was kept. The masters kept the discipline. There’s no discipline anymore. If you didn’t do something right — I was playing in a house band with Sonny Stitt, amazing gig for two weeks. He didn’t like what the drummer was doing and made him play up on the bell for two weeks. His arm is out like that for two weeks, killing him. They…

Do you feel like you’ve done your best to alleviate that? Because I watched a number of your videos and you were being the master in these situations with college students. It may seem like a small thing against the culture that is happening now but I guess I’m just trying to say that I appreciate that you share your considered opinions.
